Let me view one reference from each top candidate.

Now I have viewed 16 unique classes. Let me compile my analysis.

**Test image features:**
- Corn leaf
- Multiple elongated pale tan/yellowish-white bleached streaks running the full length of the leaf, parallel to veins
- Green areas remain between streaks
- No pustules, no circular spots, no freckles

**Comparison summary:**
- **Stewart's Disease (ref 72)**: Very strong match — pale bleached streaks running lengthwise along the leaf, green areas between, identical pattern
- **Goss's Wilt**: Large blotchy tan/brown areas with wavy edges and dark freckles — doesn't match
- **Northern Leaf Blight**: Discrete cigar-shaped lesions — not the continuous streak pattern seen
- **Gray Leaf Spot**: Short rectangular vein-bounded lesions — doesn't match
- **Maize Streak Virus**: Very fine, dense fine streaking — finer and denser than the test image
- **Maize Chlorotic Dwarf Virus**: Yellow blotchy patches with vein banding — doesn't match
- All others (Common Rust, Tar Spot, Eyespot, Carbonum, Holcus, Physoderma, Anthracnose, etc.) clearly don't match

Stewart's Disease ref 72 is by far the closest visual match to the test image — both show the characteristic pale bleached streaks running the length of the leaf with green tissue between them.
